We implemented Jenkins-based CI for gkeyll in ci/jenkins/. I'd like to explore two possible reporting improvements:
1. The current model sends a commit status to GitHub indicating if the checks passed or fail. What are the limitations on that status? could it include a list of the failed tests?
2. I'd like to add a command to CLI (each CLI script for personal/cluster/team, the gkeyll-ci.sh, and the gkeyll jeci wrapper) which provides more information on a specific build, so for example something that allows us to do "info --build 6" and it would display the same information that "recent" provides for a specific build in addition to: the reason it failed (and if it failed during runregression you could use "../gkylsoft/gkeyll/bin/gkeyll querydb" I think) and a list of artifacts available.

I’ll inspect the CI scripts and Jenkins reporting flow, then map what GitHub statuses can carry and outline the safest implementation path for a per-build `info` command. I’m using the repository’s directory-structure guidance because this is a CI layout exploration.

A GitHub commit status cannot practically carry a failed-test list. It has only a state, context, short description, and optional link; GitHub explicitly positions `target_url` as the link to full build output. It also limits each SHA/context to 1,000 posted statuses. [GitHub commit-status API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/statuses?apiVersion=2022-11-28)

Your CI currently posts only `state`, `context`, and `description`—no `target_url`—in the cluster pipelines ([Perlmutter](file:///Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile.perlmutter_gpu:156)) and personal pipeline ([personal](file:///Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/jenkinsfile.personal:63)). It would be worthwhile to add a per-build Jenkins URL as `target_url` (where that URL is reachable by PR readers). Keep the description to a terse summary, e.g. “C regression: 3 failures; see build details.”

For a GitHub-native failed-test list, migrate the reporter to a GitHub App-backed Check Run. Checks support Markdown summaries and annotations (up to 50 annotations per request), but write access is restricted to GitHub Apps—not a normal PAT/OAuth credential. [GitHub Checks API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/runs?apiVersion=2022-11-28)

`info --build 6` is very feasible and is the better place for complete diagnostics. I recommend:

```text
gkeyll-ci.sh stellar_cpu info --build 6
BUILD #6 FAILURE queue=... started=... duration=... url=...
Selectors: pr=... candidate=... baseline=...
Failure: Run C regressions (SLURM)
Regression failures:
  gyrokinetic/foo [fail]
  vlasov/bar [timeout]
Artifacts:
  ci-regression-summary.txt
  gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/gyrokinetic/regressiondb
  slurm-regression-12345.out
  ...
```

Implementation shape:

- Add `info` to `gkeyll-ci.sh` and all four platform clients.
- Fetch one Jenkins build record, including parameters and `artifacts[fileName,relativePath]`; Jenkins exposes per-build remote API data specifically for this purpose. [Jenkins Remote API](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/using/remote-access-api/)
- Reuse the existing compact `recent` formatter for the first line.
- Print artifact names and download URLs as `BUILD_URL/artifact/<relativePath>`.
- For C regressions, download the archived candidate `regressiondb` to a temporary directory and run the local `gkeyll querydb` against it. The databases are already archived in all pipelines; cluster CI also retains Slurm outputs/statuses and baseline databases.
- For non-regression failures, report the failed Pipeline stage plus a bounded tail/link to the Jenkins console or relevant archived log.

One improvement is needed to make “reason it failed” reliable: write and archive a small `ci-failure-summary.txt` containing the stage, failure class, and regression-failure paths. Parsing console output alone is fragile. The current regression helper prints exact failed tests but only persists aggregate counts in `ci-regression-summary.txt` ([checker](file:///Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/ci/jenkins/check_regression_results.lua:1)).

I would keep `info` successful when it retrieves a failed build—its job is reporting, not reproducing `status`’s failure exit code.

Ok, please create a plan for this. I would add one thing if possible: It'd be nice to have, if available, the directory to baseline and candidate results, for example something like:
  Regression failures:
    gyrokinetic/foo [fail]
    vlasov/bar [timeout]
  Baseline results dir: <baseline_results_directory>
  Candidate results dir: <candidate_results_directory>
  Artifacts dir: <artifacts_directory>
  Artifacts:
    ci-regression-summary.txt

The candidate workspace is deleted after each Pipeline run, so those original result directories will normally no longer exist when `info` is invoked. The retained equivalent is the archived artifact path (and Jenkins download URL); preserving workspaces would be a separate retention/security decision.

<proposed_plan>
# Jenkins CI build-information command

## Summary

Add `info --build NUMBER` to all CI entrypoints: `gkeyll-ci.sh`, the four platform clients, and `gkeyll jeci`. It will report the same build metadata as `recent`, a reliable archived failure summary, regression failures when queryable, and retained artifacts with their Jenkins download location. GitHub reporting changes are explicitly out of scope.

## Key changes

- Extend CLI help, dispatch, and validation with:
  ```text
  gkeyll-ci.sh <platform> info --build NUMBER
  gkeyll jeci <platform> info --build NUMBER
  ```
  `info` returns success when it successfully retrieves a build, including a failed build; retrieval or argument errors remain nonzero.

- Have each platform client request the per-build Jenkins JSON record, including build state, timestamps/duration, parameter selectors, build URL, and archived artifact paths. Print:
  ```text
  BUILD #6 FAILURE queue=... <timestamp> pr=... candidate=... baseline=... url=...
  Failure: <stage>: <message>
  Regression failures:
    gyrokinetic/foo [fail]
    vlasov/bar [timeout]
  Artifacts URL: <build-url>/artifact/
  Artifacts:
    ci-regression-summary.txt  <artifact-download-url>
    ...
  ```
  Omit unavailable sections cleanly; never report deleted candidate or baseline workspace paths.

- Add a small, always-archived `ci-failure-summary.txt` to the trusted pipelines. It records the terminal Jenkins result, the tracked failing stage, and a concise sanitized exception message. Track stage names explicitly in the Personal pipeline and the two Slurm pipelines; team-workstation inherits the Personal pipeline behavior.

- For retained candidate `*/regressiondb` artifacts, `info` downloads databases to a secure temporary directory and invokes the installed helper as:
  ```text
  <repo>/../gkylsoft/gkeyll/bin/gkeyll queryrdb --db <artifact> query --id 1 --fail-only
  ```
  Prefix emitted test names with the artifact’s solver layer. If the helper or a database is unavailable, retain the failure summary and print a short diagnostic rather than failing `info`. (`queryrdb` is the implemented command name.)

- Archive `ci-failure-summary.txt` alongside the existing logs, Slurm outputs, regression databases, and timing/selection files. Preserve current artifact retention and workspace deletion behavior.

## Test plan

- Run Bash syntax validation for all changed clients and Lua syntax/loading validation for `jeci.lua`.
- Exercise CLI parsing/help for every entrypoint, including invalid/missing build numbers.
- Use mocked Jenkins build JSON and artifact endpoints to verify successful, running, failed, missing-artifact, and inaccessible-`queryrdb` output.
- Verify regression database extraction produces only latest-run failed statuses and that temporary downloads are removed.
- Verify every Pipeline archives a failure summary on an injected stage failure and that a successful build does not claim a failure reason.

## Assumptions

- Jenkins artifact URLs are the portable “artifacts directory” representation; controller filesystem archive paths are not exposed.
- `info` is build-only; queue inspection remains the responsibility of `status`/`follow`.
- No GitHub commit-status or Check Run changes are part of this work.
</proposed_plan>

I'm in overall agreement with this plan. I just want to understand and possibly refine something. The info command will print

Artifacts URL: <build-url>/artifact/

I be able to see that directory from my terminal, e.g. with "ls <build-url>/artifact/" ? if not, what are some options to be able to see the artifact directory from the terminal (since I'm using CLI after all, I'd rather not be forced to switch to a browser)

No. `ls` only lists filesystem paths; `https://…/artifact/` is an HTTP endpoint. `curl <build-url>/artifact/` would fetch Jenkins’s HTML artifact page, not a clean directory listing.

The planned `info` command already gives the CLI-native answer: it uses the Jenkins JSON API to list artifact-relative paths and download URLs. We can make it fully terminal-friendly by printing a copyable download command per artifact, or adding e.g.:

```text
gkeyll jeci stellar_cpu artifact --build 6 --path ci-regression-summary.txt
```

which streams/downloads one artifact using the existing Jenkins credentials.

A controller-local archive path is another option—usually under `JENKINS_HOME/jobs/.../builds/6/archive/`—but it is implementation-specific, differs for nested team jobs, and is only usable when your terminal can access that controller filesystem. I would not make it the default interface.

I like the idea of an "artifact" command, I suggest it has options like
--list: list available artifacts.
--fetch: downloads all artifacts to a folder (whose name includes the build number).
--only: allows us to specify a single artifact to download, or a comma-separated list of artifacts.
--dir: optional name of folder to download artifacts into

That gives the CLI a clean separation: `info` summarizes a build, while `artifact` performs authenticated listing and retrieval without requiring a browser. I’ll refine the plan around that interface.

questions.question: How should `artifact` behave when only `--build NUMBER` is supplied, and how should `--only` combine with `--fetch`?

options.label: List by default (Recommended)
options.description: `--build N` and `--list` list; `--fetch [--only names]` downloads, with `--only` requiring `--fetch`.

options.label: Fetch by default
options.description: `--build N` downloads everything; `--list` lists and `--only` narrows the default download.

options.label: Only explicit modes
options.description: Require exactly one of `--list` or `--fetch`; permit `--only` only with `--fetch`.

questions.question: For `--fetch`, should artifacts keep their Jenkins-relative directory hierarchy locally?

options.label: Preserve hierarchy (Recommended)
options.description: Avoid basename collisions; default target is `gkeyll-ci-build-<N>/` in the current directory.

options.label: Flatten names
options.description: Place every artifact directly in the destination folder; reject collisions.

options.label: Single folder tree
options.description: Flatten by default, but add a future option to preserve paths.

result.output: {"answers":{"download_layout":{"answers":["Preserve hierarchy (Recommended)"]},"artifact_syntax":{"answers":["None of the above","user_note: I'd think --build N is always required. Then --build N can be followed by --fetch, or --fetch --dir, or --fetch --dir --only, or --fetch --only. Also, I'd like to change --dir in favor of --output-dir"]}}}

content.text: Understood: `--build N` is mandatory; fetching is opt-in; the destination flag is `--output-dir`; and downloads preserve artifact-relative paths. That implies `artifact --build N` should list by default, with `--list` retained as an explicit equivalent. One remaining safety choice is what to do if the default or requested output directory already exists.

questions.question: What should `artifact --fetch` do when its output directory already exists?

options.label: Refuse (Recommended)
options.description: Avoid mixing builds or overwriting files; ask for a new `--output-dir`.

options.label: Merge safely
options.description: Create missing paths but reject any artifact whose destination already exists.

options.label: Overwrite files
options.description: Replace matching artifact files in the chosen directory.

questions.question: Should `--list` remain as an explicit alias for the default listing behavior?

options.label: Keep alias (Recommended)
options.description: Both `artifact --build 6` and `artifact --build 6 --list` list artifacts.

options.label: Require --list
options.description: `artifact --build 6` is invalid; listing must be explicit.

options.label: Drop --list
options.description: Listing is only the default; reserve flags for fetching.

<proposed_plan>
# Jenkins CI build inspection and artifact retrieval

## Summary

Add two build-only CLI commands across `gkeyll-ci.sh`, all platform clients, and `gkeyll jeci`:

```text
info --build NUMBER
artifact --build NUMBER [--list | --fetch [--only PATH[,PATH...]] [--output-dir DIR]]
```

`info` reports the build, archived failure reason, regression failures when queryable, and available artifacts. `artifact` lists or downloads retained artifacts through Jenkins using the existing authenticated CLI path. GitHub reporting remains unchanged.

## Key changes

- Add `info --build NUMBER`:
  - Print the existing `recent`-style build metadata, failure summary when present, regression failures extracted from candidate `regressiondb` artifacts using `gkeyll queryrdb --db … query --id 1 --fail-only`, and artifact-relative paths.
  - Print `Artifacts URL: <build-url>/artifact/` as a reference, but make no browser interaction necessary.
  - Return zero after successfully reporting any retained build, including a failed build.

- Add `artifact --build NUMBER`:
  - `--build` is required and must be a positive integer.
  - Default behavior and `--list` both list every artifact with its relative path and authenticated download URL.
  - `--fetch` downloads all artifacts.
  - `--only path[,path…]` is valid only with `--fetch`, selects exact Jenkins artifact-relative paths, and rejects requested paths not present in the build.
  - `--output-dir DIR` is valid only with `--fetch`; its default is `gkeyll-ci-build-<NUMBER>` below the current directory.
  - Preserve Jenkins artifact-relative directory hierarchy beneath the output directory. Refuse the fetch if that directory already exists; validate paths before creating it and reject unsafe paths.
  - Authenticate all metadata and downloads through the current Jenkins credential mechanism; do not expose tokens in output or shell history.

- Add and archive `ci-failure-summary.txt` in the Personal, Stellar, and Perlmutter trusted Pipelines. It records terminal result, explicitly tracked failing stage, and sanitized concise failure message; team-workstation inherits the Personal workflow. Retain existing artifact policies and workspace deletion.

- Update `gkeyll/lua/Tool/jeci.lua` to recognize and forward both commands, including help rewriting. Document `info` and `artifact` in the common Jenkins README and platform usage text.

## Test plan

- Validate Bash and Lua syntax, help, dispatch, option conflicts, missing values, invalid build numbers, and `jeci` forwarding.
- Use mocked authenticated Jenkins build/artifact endpoints to cover listing, complete fetch, selected fetch, absent selection, existing output directory, malformed artifact path, and download failure cleanup.
- Verify `info` for success, running, ordinary stage failure, regression failure, absent regression database, and unavailable `queryrdb`.
- Inject Pipeline failures to verify `ci-failure-summary.txt` is archived and identifies the failing stage; verify it does not falsely report a failure for successful builds.

## Assumptions

- Jenkins artifact URLs are the portable artifact-directory representation; controller-local archive filesystem paths are not reported.
- Candidate and baseline workspaces remain deleted after archival.
- The implemented command name is `queryrdb`; `querydb` is not used.
</proposed_plan>

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared build-information and artifact helpers for Jenkins CI clients.
+
+ci_build_payload() {
+    local build_number="$1"
+    curl_auth "$(ci_build_url "$build_number")/api/json?tree=number,queueId,building,result,timestamp,duration,url,actions[parameters[name,value]],artifacts[fileName,relativePath]"
+}
+
+ci_artifact_records() {
+    local build_number="$1" payload="$2"
+    python3 -c '
+import json
+import sys
+import urllib.parse
+
+base = sys.argv[1].rstrip("/")
+for artifact in json.load(sys.stdin).get("artifacts", []):
+    path = artifact.get("relativePath")
+    if isinstance(path, str) and path:
+        print("{}\t{}/artifact/{}".format(path, base, urllib.parse.quote(path, safe="/")))
+' "$(ci_build_url "$build_number")" <<< "$payload"
+}
+
+ci_print_build() {
+    local payload="$1"
+    python3 -c '
+import datetime
+import json
+import sys
+
+build = json.load(sys.stdin)
+values = {}
+for action in build.get("actions") or []:
+    for parameter in action.get("parameters") or []:
+        name = parameter.get("name")
+        if name in ("CANDIDATE_PR", "CANDIDATE_REF", "BASELINE_REF"):
+            values[name] = parameter.get("value") or "-"
+timestamp = build.get("timestamp")
+when = "-" if timestamp is None else datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
+    timestamp / 1000.0, datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
+state = "RUNNING" if build.get("building", False) else (build.get("result") or "UNKNOWN")
+print("BUILD #{number} {state} queue={queue} {when} pr={pr} candidate={candidate} baseline={baseline} url={url}".format(
+    number=build.get("number", "?"), state=state,
+    queue=build.get("queueId") if build.get("queueId") is not None else "-",
+    when=when, pr=values.get("CANDIDATE_PR", "-"),
+    candidate=values.get("CANDIDATE_REF", "-"),
+    baseline=values.get("BASELINE_REF", "-"), url=build.get("url", "-")))
+' <<< "$payload"
+}
+
+ci_artifact_url() {
+    local build_number="$1" artifact_path="$2"
+    python3 -c 'import sys, urllib.parse; print(sys.argv[1].rstrip("/") + "/artifact/" + urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[2], safe="/"))' \
+        "$(ci_build_url "$build_number")" "$artifact_path"
+}
+
+ci_safe_artifact_path() {
+    local artifact_path="$1" component
+    [[ -n "$artifact_path" && "$artifact_path" != /* && "$artifact_path" != *'//' ]] || return 1
+    IFS=/ read -r -a components <<< "$artifact_path"
+    for component in "${components[@]}"; do
+        [[ -n "$component" && "$component" != . && "$component" != .. ]] || return 1
+    done
+}
+
+ci_download_artifact() {
+    local build_number="$1" artifact_path="$2" destination="$3"
+    curl_auth --output "$destination" "$(ci_artifact_url "$build_number" "$artifact_path")"
+}
+
+ci_print_failure_summary() {
+    local build_number="$1" payload="$2" record artifact_path artifact_url temporary
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r artifact_path artifact_url; do
+        [[ "$artifact_path" == ci-failure-summary.txt ]] || continue
+        temporary="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gkeyll-ci-failure.XXXXXX")"
+        if ci_download_artifact "$build_number" "$artifact_path" "$temporary"; then
+            local stage='' message='' result='' key value
+            while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
+                case "$key" in
+                    stage) stage="$value" ;;
+                    message) message="$value" ;;
+                    result) result="$value" ;;
+                esac
+            done < "$temporary"
+            rm -f "$temporary"
+            echo "Failure: ${stage:-unknown}: ${message:-${result:-unknown failure}}"
+        else
+            rm -f "$temporary"
+            echo 'Failure: CI failure summary artifact could not be downloaded.'
+        fi
+        return
+    done < <(ci_artifact_records "$build_number" "$payload")
+}
+
+ci_print_regression_failures() {
+    local build_number="$1" payload="$2" queryrdb record artifact_path artifact_url temporary layer output found=false
+    queryrdb="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../gkylsoft/gkeyll/bin/gkeyll"
+    [[ -x "$queryrdb" ]] || {
+        echo "Regression failures: queryrdb is unavailable at $queryrdb"
+        return
+    }
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r artifact_path artifact_url; do
+        [[ "$artifact_path" =~ ^gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/(.*/)?(moments|vlasov|gyrokinetic|pkpm)/regressiondb$ ]] || continue
+        layer="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
+        temporary="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gkeyll-ci-regressiondb.XXXXXX")"
+        if ! ci_download_artifact "$build_number" "$artifact_path" "$temporary"; then
+            rm -f "$temporary"
+            echo "Regression failures: could not download $artifact_path"
+            continue
+        fi
+        if output="$("$queryrdb" queryrdb --db "$temporary" query --id 1 --fail-only 2>/dev/null)"; then
+            while IFS= read -r record; do
+                if [[ "$record" =~ ^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+(.+)[[:space:]]+(fail|timeout|compile_fail|no_output|crash)[[:space:]] ]]; then
+                    if [[ "$found" == false ]]; then
+                        echo 'Regression failures:'
+                        found=true
+                    fi
+                    echo "  $layer/${BASH_REMATCH[1]} [${BASH_REMATCH[2]}]"
+                fi
+            done <<< "$output"
+        else
+            echo "Regression failures: queryrdb could not inspect $artifact_path"
+        fi
+        rm -f "$temporary"
+    done < <(ci_artifact_records "$build_number" "$payload")
+}
+
+ci_info_command() {
+    [[ $# -eq 2 && "$1" == --build ]] || die 'usage: info --build NUMBER'
+    positive 'build number' "$2"
+    local payload
+    payload="$(ci_build_payload "$2")" || die "Build #$2 is not available"
+    ci_print_build "$payload"
+    ci_print_failure_summary "$2" "$payload"
+    ci_print_regression_failures "$2" "$payload"
+    echo "Artifacts URL: $(ci_build_url "$2")/artifact/"
+    echo 'Artifacts:'
+    local artifact_path artifact_url found=false
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r artifact_path artifact_url; do
+        echo "  $artifact_path  $artifact_url"
+        found=true
+    done < <(ci_artifact_records "$2" "$payload")
+    [[ "$found" == true ]] || echo '  (none)'
+}
+
+ci_artifact_command() {
+    local build_number='' mode=list only='' output_dir=''
+    while (($#)); do
+        case "$1" in
+            --build) (($# >= 2)) || die '--build requires a number'; build_number="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+            --list) [[ "$mode" == list ]] || die '--list cannot be combined with --fetch'; shift ;;
+            --fetch) [[ "$mode" == list ]] || die '--fetch cannot be repeated'; mode=fetch; shift ;;
+            --only) (($# >= 2)) || die '--only requires one or more artifact paths'; only="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+            --output-dir) (($# >= 2)) || die '--output-dir requires a directory'; output_dir="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+            *) die "unknown artifact option: $1" ;;
+        esac
+    done
+    [[ -n "$build_number" ]] || die 'usage: artifact --build NUMBER [--list | --fetch [--only PATH[,PATH...]] [--output-dir DIR]]'
+    positive 'build number' "$build_number"
+    [[ "$mode" == fetch || -z "$only$output_dir" ]] || die '--only and --output-dir require --fetch'
+
+    local payload
+    payload="$(ci_build_payload "$build_number")" || die "Build #$build_number is not available"
+    if [[ "$mode" == list ]]; then
+        local artifact_path artifact_url found=false
+        while IFS=$'\t' read -r artifact_path artifact_url; do
+            echo "$artifact_path  $artifact_url"
+            found=true
+        done < <(ci_artifact_records "$build_number" "$payload")
+        [[ "$found" == true ]] || echo 'No archived artifacts.'
+        return
+    fi
+
+    [[ -n "$output_dir" ]] || output_dir="gkeyll-ci-build-$build_number"
+    [[ ! -e "$output_dir" ]] || die "output directory already exists: $output_dir"
+    local -a available=() selected=() requested=()
+    local artifact_path artifact_url requested_path
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r artifact_path artifact_url; do
+        ci_safe_artifact_path "$artifact_path" || die "Jenkins returned unsafe artifact path: $artifact_path"
+        available+=("$artifact_path")
+    done < <(ci_artifact_records "$build_number" "$payload")
+    if [[ -n "$only" ]]; then
+        IFS=, read -r -a requested <<< "$only"
+        for requested_path in "${requested[@]}"; do
+            [[ -n "$requested_path" ]] || die '--only contains an empty artifact path'
+            local match=false
+            for artifact_path in "${available[@]}"; do
+                [[ "$artifact_path" == "$requested_path" ]] || continue
+                selected+=("$artifact_path")
+                match=true
+                break
+            done
+            [[ "$match" == true ]] || die "artifact is not available in build #$build_number: $requested_path"
+        done
+    else
+        selected=("${available[@]}")
+    fi
+    ((${#selected[@]})) || die "Build #$build_number has no archived artifacts"
+
+    mkdir -p "$output_dir"
+    for artifact_path in "${selected[@]}"; do
+        local destination="$output_dir/$artifact_path"
+        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
+        if ! ci_download_artifact "$build_number" "$artifact_path" "$destination"; then
+            rm -rf "$output_dir"
+            die "could not download artifact: $artifact_path"
+        fi
+        echo "Downloaded $artifact_path"
+    done
+    echo "Artifacts downloaded to: $output_dir"
+}

content.text: Implementation and focused verification are complete. The only checks not run are live Jenkins/Pipeline executions and a real regression-database query, because they require the configured controllers and machine environments.

Implemented the CI reporting and artifact CLI.

Highlights:

- Added `info --build N` and `artifact --build N` to all platform clients, `gkeyll-ci.sh`, and `gkeyll jeci`.
- `artifact` supports default/`--list`, `--fetch`, `--only PATH[,PATH…]`, and `--output-dir DIR`; downloads preserve artifact hierarchy and refuse an existing destination.
- Added archived `ci-failure-summary.txt` with failing stage and concise error reason in Personal, Stellar, and Perlmutter pipelines.
- `info` lists artifacts, reports the summary, and queries candidate regression databases when `queryrdb` is available.
- Updated Jenkins CI documentation and examples.

Verification passed:

- Bash syntax checks for all affected scripts.
- Lua syntax check for `gkeyll/lua/Tool/jeci.lua`.
- CLI help/dispatch checks.
- Mocked Jenkins artifact listing, selective download, and existing-output-directory rejection.
- `git diff --check`.

Live Jenkins/Pipeline runs were not performed because they require configured controllers and cluster environments.
Will all personal/cluster/team machines write out ci-failure-summary.txt ?

Yes—for any build that reaches its Jenkins workspace and completes Pipeline cleanup:

- Personal: writes and archives `ci-failure-summary.txt` on failure.
- Team workstation: uses the Personal trusted workflow, so same behavior.
- Stellar CPU and Perlmutter GPU: write and archive it on failure.

It will not exist for successful builds, or failures before a workspace is allocated (for example, invalid top-level Jenkins configuration). It also cannot be retained if artifact archival itself fails.
